claims.explanation: ICI-162846 is annotated as an HRH2 (histamine H2 receptor) antagonist, but its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is not explained by HRH2 blockade alone. The most plausible genomic selectivity is synthetic lethality with loss of NF2/merlin or PTEN, both of which converge on PI3K/AKT/mTOR and Hippo/YAP signaling and are enriched in the sensitive lines, while PIK3CA/BRAF/NRAS-activated lines are relatively protected. TP53 mutation is common in both groups and is therefore not a strong selective feature.

features.basis: Enriched in sensitive lines (YD8, BICR6, SNU410, NCIH2052); merlin loss activates YAP/PI3K-mTOR stress signaling
Recurrent in sensitive lines (786O, TE4, H4, KALS1, NCIH1339); PTEN loss increases PI3K/AKT/mTOR dependence
Enriched in least-affected lines (SNU719, HGC27, RT112, KYSE510, MDAMB361); constitutive PI3K activation may bypass the drug's effect
Present in least-affected lines (WM793, MDAMB361, OV90) and CAL12T; MAPK activation may confer resistance
Seen in least-affected SNU719 and SW1088; RAS/MAPK activation may reduce sensitivity
Very common in sensitive lines but also frequent in resistant lines, so weak and likely not selective
Annotated drug target; higher HRH2 expression could increase dependence on H2-receptor signaling
